paragraphs.title: The Vision’s Heading and the Future World Center

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.”
easy.q: Who saw the word concerning Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: At the beginning of the chapter
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “And it shall come to pass in the last days.”
easy.q: When shall the mountain of the Lord’s house be established?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says that “all nations shall flow unto it.”

answers: To learn his ways and walk in his paths
medium.explanation: Verse 3 says, “he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.”
medium.q: Why will many people go to the mountain of the Lord?

answers: They will come toward it in great numbers
medium.explanation: The nations are pictured as moving toward the Lord’s mountain in large numbers.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “flow unto it” suggest?

answers: They will be hidden in caves
They will be given to kings
medium.explanation: Verse 4 says swords will become plowshares and spears will become pruninghooks.
medium.q: What will happen to swords and spears?

challenge.explanation: Verse 3 says, “out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”
challenge.q: What place is presented as the source of the law and the word of the Lord?

answers: War will give way to productive work
challenge.explanation: The change from swords and spears to farming tools represents peace and useful labor.
challenge.q: What does the transformation of weapons symbolize?

answers: A spiritual center, teaching, judgment, and peace
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the Lord’s mountain, instruction, judgment among nations, and the end of war.

paragraphs.title: The Call to the House of Jacob and Its Departure from the Path

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.”
easy.q: Who is called to walk in the light of the Lord?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Their land also is full of silver and gold.”
easy.q: What filled the land according to verse 7?

answers: The work of their own hands
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “they worship the work of their own hands.”

medium.explanation: Verses 7–8 mention silver, gold, horses, chariots, and idols.
medium.q: Which things are listed alongside the wealth of the land?

medium.explanation: The word describes people practicing divination or occult prediction.

answers: They accompany foreign customs and misplaced trust
They bring peace among the nations
They are used to teach the Lord’s ways
medium.explanation: The passage connects them with foreign influence, military strength, and idols.
medium.q: Why are wealth and horses presented negatively in this passage?

answers: Walking in the Lord’s light versus following foreign ways
Learning peace versus making farming tools
challenge.explanation: Verse 5 calls Jacob to walk in the Lord’s light, while the following verses describe foreign practices, wealth, power, and idols.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between verse 5 and verses 6–8?

answers: It is filled with material wealth and idols rather than the Lord’s light
It contains only people learning the law
challenge.explanation: The land is full of silver, gold, horses, chariots, and idols, showing misplaced priorities.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement that the land is “full” emphasize?

answers: They represent reliance on material things or human works
They are sources of the Lord’s law
challenge.explanation: They are presented as signs of dependence on possessions, military power, and man-made objects.
challenge.q: What do wealth, horses, and idols have in common in this description?

paragraphs.title: Human Humiliation Before the Revelation of the Lord

answers: They bow down and humble themselves
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself.”
easy.q: What happens to the mean man and the great man?

answers: Because of the fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty
easy.explanation: Verse 10 mentions “the fear of the Lord” and “the glory of his majesty.”
Verse 11 says, “the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.”
easy.q: Who alone shall be exalted in that day?

answers: The day of the Lord and the revelation of his majesty
medium.explanation: The passage connects human humiliation with the day of the Lord and his glory.
medium.q: What brings human pride low according to these verses?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the lowering of those who are proud and lofty.
medium.q: What does “brought low” mean in this passage?

answers: It exposes human pride and exalts the Lord alone
medium.explanation: Verses 11–12 say that proud and lofty people will be brought low, while the Lord alone is exalted.
medium.q: How does the day of the Lord relate to human pride?

answers: Only the Lord will remain exalted
challenge.explanation: “The Lord alone” emphasizes the unique and unrivaled exaltation of the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the word “alone” emphasize in verse 11?

answers: Human pride that will be humbled
challenge.explanation: The expression symbolizes proud attitudes that will be brought down.
The verses describe people being humbled and hiding because of fear and majesty.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the human response to the Lord’s revelation?

paragraphs.title: The Humbling of Nature and Human Power

answers: The cedars of Lebanon and the oaks of Bashan
easy.explanation: Verse 13 names “the cedars of Lebanon” and “the oaks of Bashan.”
Verse 15 mentions “every high tower” and “every fenced wall.”
Verse 17 repeats that “the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.”
easy.q: Who alone shall be exalted at the end of the passage?

answers: Trees, mountains, hills, towers, walls, and ships
medium.explanation: Verses 13–16 list natural features, human structures, ships, and pleasant pictures.
medium.q: What kinds of things will be brought low before the Lord?

medium.explanation: A fenced wall is a protected or fortified wall.

answers: To show that every kind of greatness is humbled before the Lord
To teach people how to build towers
medium.explanation: Trees, mountains, towers, walls, and ships all represent impressive forms of natural or human power.
medium.q: Why are both nature and human structures mentioned?

answers: They represent height, strength, or greatness
They are all made of metal
challenge.explanation: The passage lists elevated and powerful things to show that they too will be humbled.
challenge.q: What do cedars, mountains, and towers have in common in the passage?

answers: It broadens the description to many forms of greatness
It limits the description to one tree
It shows that these things will remain exalted
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording creates an extensive list of natural and human powers facing the day of the Lord.
challenge.q: What is the effect of repeatedly using “upon all”?

answers: Both nature and human achievements will be humbled
The prophet is speaking only about farming
The prophet is changing from peace to teaching
challenge.explanation: The list includes both created features and structures built by people.
challenge.q: What does the movement from trees and mountains to towers and walls suggest?

paragraphs.title: The Abolition of Idols and Humanity’s Hiding

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says, “And the idols he shall utterly abolish.”
easy.q: What will happen to the idols?

answers: His idols of silver and gold
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says a man will cast away his silver and golden idols.
easy.q: What will a man cast away?

answers: In holes, caves, and clefts of the rocks
On the mountain of the Lord
easy.explanation: Verses 19 and 21 describe holes, caves, clefts, and the tops of ragged rocks.
easy.q: Where will people try to hide?

answers: Because of fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty
Because they want to make the idols more valuable
Because the idols teach the law
medium.explanation: The action occurs in response to the Lord’s fearsome majesty.
medium.q: Why will people cast away their silver and golden idols?

medium.explanation: “Utterly abolish” means to remove or destroy completely.

answers: Both show people abandoning former security before the fear of the Lord
Both describe the building of a new city
medium.explanation: People discard their idols and seek shelter because the Lord’s majesty has overcome their former confidence.
medium.q: What is the connection between casting away idols and hiding in rocks?

answers: Wealth that has become an object of worship
The source of the Lord’s law
challenge.explanation: The idols can represent material wealth that people have treated as worthy of worship.
challenge.q: What may the silver and golden idols symbolize in the passage?

answers: The revelation of the Lord destroys confidence in former objects of worship
People receive the idols from other nations
challenge.explanation: When the Lord rises in majesty, the idols lose their authority and value.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by casting away the idols “in that day”?

answers: Casting away idols, hiding, and fear
challenge.explanation: The passage describes people throwing away idols and hiding from the Lord’s majesty.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the people’s response?

paragraphs.title: The Conclusion: Cease from Trusting in Man

easy.q: From whom does the verse say to cease?

easy.explanation: The verse describes man as one “whose breath is in his nostrils.”

answers: As the source of the law
easy.explanation: The question “wherein is he to be accounted of?” challenges the idea of human greatness.
easy.q: How does the verse describe man’s importance?

answers: His breath is in his nostrils
medium.explanation: The verse points to man’s breath as a reminder of his limited and dependent nature.
medium.q: Why should man not be regarded as absolutely important?

answers: How much should he be regarded or valued?
How much money does he have?
medium.explanation: The question asks about the measure of man’s true importance.
medium.q: What does “wherein is he to be accounted of?” mean?

answers: It warns against relying on man and redirects attention to the Lord
It calls people to build more idols
medium.explanation: After describing human pride, idols, and power being humbled, the verse warns against trusting in man.
medium.q: How does verse 22 summarize the chapter?

answers: His breath shows his mortality and dependence
His breath proves that man is divine
challenge.explanation: The mention of breath highlights that man is temporary, limited, and dependent.
challenge.q: What is the connection between man’s breath and the conclusion about his importance?

answers: Man is limited and humbled, while the Lord alone is exalted
Man is exalted while the Lord hides
Man teaches the law while the Lord builds chariots
challenge.explanation: The chapter repeatedly humbles humanity and declares that the Lord alone will be exalted.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between man and the Lord in this chapter?

answers: Do not treat man as ultimate or trust his power instead of the Lord
Leave the mountain of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The command summarizes the warning against human pride, wealth, power, and idols in contrast with the Lord’s greatness.
challenge.q: What does “Cease ye from man” mean in the context of the chapter?
